blocks.text: Imagine building a skyscraper without blueprints or a plan. Software development can be just as complex, requiring structured processes to ensure success.

blocks.markdown: Software development processes are essential for managing the complexity of building non-trivial software systems. They provide a framework for organizing tasks, resources, and timelines to deliver high-quality software.

blocks.title: Software Process
blocks.text: A software process is a set of activities and associated results that produce a software product. It includes phases such as requirements gathering, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance.

blocks.markdown: Let's explore three major software process models: Waterfall, Iterative, and Agile. Each has distinct characteristics and is suited to different types of projects.

blocks.title: Waterfall Model
blocks.text: The Waterfall model is a linear and sequential approach where each phase must be completed before the next begins. It's best for projects with well-understood requirements.

blocks.title: Iterative Model
blocks.text: The Iterative model develops the system through repeated cycles (iterations) and in smaller portions at a time, allowing for feedback and refinement.

blocks.title: Agile Model
blocks.text: Agile is a flexible and adaptive model that emphasizes customer collaboration and responsiveness to change, often using frameworks like Scrum or Kanban.

blocks.markdown: Each process model involves several key activities. Understanding these activities is crucial for selecting the right model for a project.

blocks.title: Key Activities
blocks.text: Typical activities in a software process include: requirements gathering, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance.

blocks.title: Choosing a Process Model
blocks.prompt: Consider a project where the requirements are unclear and likely to change. Which process model would be most suitable?

steps.text: Identify the characteristics of the project: unclear and changing requirements.
Match these characteristics with the process model that best accommodates them.
steps.latex: Agile \text{ is suitable for projects with dynamic and changing requirements.}

blocks.answer: The Agile model is most suitable for this project.

blocks.title: Applying the Waterfall Model
blocks.prompt: A project has well-defined requirements and a fixed deadline. How would the Waterfall model be applied?

steps.text: Begin with the requirements gathering phase, ensuring all requirements are documented.
Proceed sequentially through design, implementation, testing, and finally maintenance.

blocks.answer: The Waterfall model would be applied in a linear fashion, completing each phase before moving to the next.

points: Software processes provide structure to software development.
Waterfall, Iterative, and Agile models have distinct characteristics and are suited to different project types.
Key activities include requirements gathering, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance.
